papers_read.title_as_printed: Associations of Antihypertensive Medication Consumption and Drug-Drug Interaction with Statin and Metformin with Reduced Alzheimer's Disease and Related Dementias Risk among Hypertensive Patients with Mild Cognitive Impairment using High Volume Claims Data
Polypharmacy and risk of dementia progression in older adults with mild cognitive impairment: A longitudinal cohort study

what_each_reports.P-999: Lundin et al., Research Square preprint rs-2629005/v1 (posted 13 April 2023). Optum claims 2007-2020: 128,683 hypertensive MCI patients (100,678 AHM users, 28,005 non-users). The Cox model is adjusted for demographics, 13 comorbidities and statin/metformin use; the outcome is incident ADRD by claims codes or two anti-dementia drug fills within 6 months. Users of each class vs non-users of that class (who may take other classes): diuretics 0.96 (0.95-0.98), beta blockers 0.98 (0.96-1.00), CCBs 0.97 (0.95-0.98), ACE inhibitors 0.98 (0.97-1.00), ARBs 0.98 (0.97-1.00). Any AHM vs no AHM: 1.06 (1.04-1.08) overall, 0.84 (0.80-0.88) among statin users and 1.11 (1.08-1.13) among statin non-users. Monotherapy class comparisons were not significant (p 0.053-0.974). Caution: the Methods print COPD codes (ICD-9 491.x/492.x/496; ICD-10 J41-J44) as the hypertension definition and list G31.83 under both MCI and ADRD. These are evidently transcription errors, since Table 1 gives COPD prevalence of 29.6-36.8%, not 100%.
what_each_reports.P-1157: Hsu et al., Alzheimer's Dement (TRCI) 2025;11:e70179. Kaohsiung veterans system: 237 MCI (CDR 0.5), median follow-up 34 months, 89 progressed to CDR 1 with neurologist confirmation (all-cause dementia). Polypharmacy (5 or more prescription drugs at baseline) gave HR 0.49 (0.31-0.78), adjusted for age, sex, CCI, education, smoking, sensory impairment, Barthel, GDS-15, MNA-SF and recruitment source; thresholds from 5 to 8 drugs were all significant. Per-category Cox models with the same covariates gave antihypertensive agents HR 0.59 (0.37-0.93) and lipid-modifying agents HR 0.43 (0.23-0.79). About 65% of the cohort was hypertensive (154/237), and hypertension was more common among those who did not progress (72.3% vs 52.8%, p = 0.003).

quantity_a: Adjusted Cox HR for incident claims-coded ADRD after the first MCI diagnosis, for users of one antihypertensive class vs non-users of that class (who may use other classes), or any AHM vs none, in a cohort restricted to hypertensive patients (US Optum claims). Exposure is consumption 'during the study period', and the model is adjusted for statin and metformin use.
quantity_b: Adjusted Cox HR for neurologist-confirmed progression from CDR 0.5 to CDR 1, for baseline polypharmacy (5 or more prescription drugs vs fewer) and, secondarily, for baseline exposure to a drug category (e.g. any antihypertensive agent) vs no exposure. The cohort is general MCI veterans in Taiwan, about 65% hypertensive; the covariates include no hypertension term and no other medications.
incompatible_if_same: Yes, for every alignment, which is why the verdict turns entirely on the quantity. The record's framing sets class-level 0.96-0.98 against polypharmacy 0.49 (0.31-0.78): same direction, disjoint intervals. The closest like-for-like figures, which the record omits, set P-1157's antihypertensive-agent HR 0.59 (0.37-0.93) against P-999's any-AHM-vs-none aHR 1.06 (1.04-1.08): opposite directions, disjoint intervals. P-1157's upper bound of 0.93 also excludes P-999's class-level estimates. If any of these were the same quantity, the results would be incompatible.

gates.task: match: T2 on both rows (exposure association with MCI-to-dementia progression).
gates.dataset_family: mismatch: Optum US claims vs the Kaohsiung Veterans General Hospital / Veterans Homes cohort; no waiver on record.
gates.validation_tier: n/a, counted as matched: two association studies, neither of which validates a model (V2 on both rows).
gates.modality_family: match at family level: both use clinical medication-exposure records (pharmacy claims vs baseline prescription records from a geriatric assessment). The registry subtype FAIL ('clinical_EHR' vs 'nomogram_clinical_scores') rests on a miscode, since P-1157 builds no nomogram.

endpoint_and_metric: The metric type is compatible (adjusted Cox HR in both) and the endpoint class is the same (MCI to all-cause dementia). Ascertainment differs: claims ICD codes or two anti-dementia drug fills within 6 months, vs CDR 1 confirmed by neurologists. Follow-up differs: Optum 2007-2020, with a mean of about 22 months to ADRD among converters, vs a median of 34 months. What differs decisively is the exposure contrast and the population behind it (see grounds).
independence: Independent: different countries, datasets and author groups; neither cites the other.
grounds: On the record's own framing the exposures differ. P-999 contrasts users of one antihypertensive class with non-users of that class; P-1157's headline contrasts a medication count (5 or more prescription drugs) with fewer.

The closest like-for-like figures, which the record omits, are P-1157's antihypertensive-agent HR 0.59 and P-999's any-AHM-vs-none aHR 1.06. They point opposite ways, but the population behind the comparison differs. P-999 is restricted to hypertensive patients, so its comparator is untreated hypertensives. P-1157 includes MCI patients without hypertension, has no hypertension covariate, and finds hypertension itself more common among those who did not progress, so its estimate cannot be separated from hypertension status.

P-999 shows how far the estimate depends on the comparator and on co-medication: 0.96-0.98 per class against non-users of that class, 1.06 for any AHM against none, 0.84 with statins and 1.11 without. P-1157's per-category models adjust for no other medication, and its exposure is a baseline prescription, whereas P-999 counts consumption 'during the study period'.
The dataset-family gate fails, with no waiver on record.
No pairing of estimates across the two papers therefore estimates the same quantity, and the numerical gaps cannot be read as a contradiction.

evidence_quotes.quote: Users of each major AHM class showed significantly lower risk of developing ADRD compared to non-users of that specific drug class (adjusted hazard ratio (aHR): 0.96-0.98; all P≤0.048).
‘ARB non-users’ refer to patients that do not take any ARBs, but may or may not consume AHMs from other drug classes.
Patients who use any form of AHMs had 6% higher adjusted hazard ratio of ADRD (95% CI: (1.04, 1.08), P < 0.001) than non-users (Table 3).
the study population was narrowed down from patients with Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI) to hypertensive patients with MCI.

Under consumption of Statins, use of any AHMs or major AHM classes except for ‘Other’ AHMs showed protective effect against ADRD risk, whereas the use showed harmful effect under non-consumption of Statins.
The study included 100,678 patients who were taking at least one class of AHM and 28,005 who were not taking any AHMs during the study period.

Cox regression analysis revealed that polypharmacy was significantly associated with a reduced risk of MCI progression to dementia (hazard ratio [HR] = 0.49, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.31 to 0.78) after adjusting for covariates.

We observed that certain medications, such as antihypertensive agents (HR = 0.59, 95% CI: 0.37 to 0.93) and lipid-modifying agents (HR = 0.43, 95% CI: 0.23 to 0.79), were significantly associated with a reduced risk of dementia progression.
adjusting for potential confounders, including age, sex, CCI, education, smoking status, hearing and visual impairment, Barthel Index Scores, GDS-15, MNA-SF, and recruitment source.
with those who remained with MCI, participants who progressed to dementia had a lower prevalence of hypertension (p = 0.003)

record_defects: The conflict_statement says P-999 'puts each antihypertensive class at adjusted HR 0.96-0.98 versus non-use', and claim_a says 'five antihypertensive classes against non-use'. P-999's comparator is non-users of that specific class, who 'may or may not consume AHMs from other drug classes'. Against non-use of any AHM the estimate is aHR 1.06 (1.04-1.08), above 1 (Table 3).

'essentially at the null' / 'puts the class effect at the null': the class-level intervals exclude 1 for diuretics and CCBs (0.95-0.98) and reach 1.00 for the others. The authors report 'significantly lower risk' (all P <= 0.048) and conclude that 'All five major AHM classes showed a protective effect'. The effects are small, but the paper does not report them as null.

'P-1157's class attribution a subgroup reading carrying no between-class test' (and claim_b): there is indeed no between-class test, but P-1157 reports adjusted per-category Cox estimates, antihypertensive agents HR 0.59 (0.37-0.93) and lipid-modifying agents HR 0.43 (0.23-0.79). The record omits them, although they are the figures a synthesis would set against P-999's class-level HRs.

residual_risk says P-999's class-level HRs are 'reported with no confidence intervals anywhere in its digest', so that the estimate 'rests on sample size alone'. The PDF prints a 95% CI for every class-level aHR (Table 3).
'a corpus estimate 600 times larger in sample': 128,683 / 237 is about 543.

The evidence quote filed under P-999 ('The results nominate common antihypertensive, statin and metformin combinations for formal drug-repurposing trials, but do not establish treatment efficacy') and claim_a's 'its own significance statement declines efficacy' have no counterpart in the PDF: there is no such sentence and no significance statement. The authors conclude that 'All five major AHM classes showed a protective effect' and ask only that the associations 'be interpreted with caution and warrant replication'.
The gate FAIL on modality_subtype rests on P-1157 being coded 'nomogram_clinical_scores', but P-1157 builds no nomogram. This concerns registry state, not a PDF contradiction.
what_would_change_the_verdict: An estimate that neither PDF contains: P-1157's antihypertensive-agent HR within its 154 hypertensive participants (treated vs untreated), adjusted for co-medication, staying below 1 with an interval that excludes P-999's any-AHM estimate of 1.06 (1.04-1.08). The two papers would then estimate the same comparison: treated vs untreated hypertension in MCI, all-cause dementia, Cox HR. A genuine verdict would still require the adjudicator to waive the dataset-family gate on record and to judge the exposure-window difference (use during follow-up vs baseline prescription), given that P-999's own estimate moves from 1.11 to 0.84 with statin co-use.
